questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute nominal rate
questions.stem: Explain the nominal rate when the real rate is four percent and inflation is three percent.

answer.exemplar: The nominal rate equals the real rate plus inflation, so four percent plus three percent gives a seven percent nominal interest rate.

questions.explanation: Nominal equals real plus inflation, so four plus three equals seven percent. Nominal rates compensate for inflation.
questions.hint: Add inflation to the real rate.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify demand-pull inflation in a boom
questions.stem: An architect's report shows demand rising faster than supply; this inflation type has how many words in its name?
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation has two words in its name. It arises when demand exceeds supply and pulls prices up.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify cost-push inflation from a supply shock
questions.stem: A material cost shock raises prices by four percent; if demand is unchanged, this is cost-push inflation of what percent?
questions.explanation: The price rise is four percent, so cost-push inflation is four percent. It stems from supply costs, not demand.
questions.hint: The price rise equals the inflation rate.
